cards.title: From answering prompts to ongoing responsibility
cards.summary: Altman introduces Dots as agents intended to know what matters to a user and act without a fresh prompt for every task.
cards.interpretation: Ongoing responsibility changes the product question: when should an agent act, interrupt or ask? This is a vendor vision, not independent evidence of reliable autonomy.
cards.opportunity: Try one reversible responsibility with a clear success check. Record useful outcomes, avoidable interruptions and moments needing permission before expanding its scope.

cards.title: A 3D leap does not prove a video-editing leap
cards.summary: Joey Daoud contrasts promising 3D work with video-editing tests that did not improve shot selection or timeline assembly in his own trials.
cards.interpretation: A striking demo in one tool does not establish equal usefulness in another. Workflow-specific judgment, interfaces and evaluation still matter. This small creator test is a counterview, not a controlled benchmark.
cards.opportunity: Test a 3D scene and a short edit separately against your own quality checklist. Log finishing time and mistakes; compare useful output rather than demo impressiveness.
